title: Global Economy Can't Afford AI Misstep, IMF Managing Director Warns
source_used: The Nation Thailand (report of the same IMF debate; MarketWatch page blocked)
key_facts: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva spoke at a debate on the global economy at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok on Thursday 15 Oct 2026.
She said the world economy is 'like on one leg', increasingly relying on AI investment, and asked what happens if it falters.
She said the IMF's 3.1% global growth forecast for 2026 masks widening differences between countries.
The United States, China and India are benefiting from AI investment, while Thailand and South Korea gain from AI supply chains.
Other economies struggle with inflation, debt and higher energy costs; she urged governments to rebuild financial buffers.
Higher food and fuel prices, possibly worsened by El Nino, could keep inflation up and raise debt-servicing costs.
quote_evidence: At a debate on the global economy, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned that the Fund’s forecast of 3.1% global growth for 2026 masked widening differences between countries.
“We have a world economy that is like on one leg,” she warned, questioning the consequences if AI investment faltered.
why_it_matters_hint: The IMF chief warns the world economy leans too heavily on AI investment.
notes: The pool item is MarketWatch's story (blocked, 401). It was not read, and its exact wording may cover a different Georgieva remark; The Nation Thailand's report of her 15 Oct debate remarks is used and credited instead.
